name: Deep
look: Submarines, spy missions, lost aircraft, rockets and the machines behind them, told in teal and orange: real archive footage in a dark monitor with a timecode, stencilled datelines over the picture, an abstract route chart of the journey, a cutaway of the vessel with the crew as glowing figures and the ones the story follows in red, a sonar screen of contacts, a classified readout of the facts, the wall map of a headquarters the camera pushes into, two-tone maps with a white route, and pictures drawn as matte 3D renders where no footage exists. No captions.
tagline: Teal and orange: stencil dates, sonar, cutaways, the map room.

devices.use: a stencilled date, place or name over the footage (the way the story stamps a time)
an abstract chart of a journey between two named points with a distance or a length

a cross-section silhouette of a vessel, aircraft, rocket, station or building (shape: submarine | ship | plane | rocket | building | tunnel) with the crew as glowing figures and the ones the story follows in red
contacts on a sweeping screen (bearing 0-360, range 0-1)
a classified file of 3-5 real facts
the wall map of a headquarters the camera pushes into, for the plan of an operation.
where it happens (the template's map colours)
a real photo of a person named, in a pool of light

rules: Every graphic shows a real fact the voice gives at that moment (a name, a date, a place, a figure, a quote) - times come from the word timing, never before the narrator says it.
Footage: every 2-th shot sits in the monitor frame (frame='monitor'); clips under 5 s, chained when a line is longer; no talking heads, influencers or logos (QC).

This is a military or technical mystery: the first minute opens on a stencil (the date or the place of the cold open), a map (two-tone) on the first place, a cutaway of the vessel, aircraft, rocket or station the story is about the first time it is named, a readout of the mission's facts within the first 40 seconds, a spotlight on the first public person named, and text labels for depths, distances, speeds and dates.

After the hook: archive footage in the monitor carries it; a route when a journey or a distance is described; a sonar when contacts, detection or pursuit are described; a cutaway when the story goes inside a machine; a readout for any list of specifications or facts; a maproom when a plan, an operation or a headquarters is described; a stencil on every new date; a map when the story moves; a spotlight on each new public person. One graphic every 20 to 30 seconds, never the same twice in a row.
DEEP: real archive footage in a dark monitor, stencil datelines, sonar, cutaways, readouts, the map room, two-tone maps, and matte 3D renders drawn where no footage exists. No captions by default.
